conventions.convention: L²₀(P) consists of real square-integrable measurable functions modulo P-almost-sure equality with expectation zero; expectation is representative-independent.

DQM paths are one-sided, indexed by 0 ≤ t < ε, through P₀=P, with one supplied sigma-finite common dominator. The root-density remainder is o(t) in L² as t decreases to zero; score centering is proved rather than assumed.
AC is the convention for simultaneous density-version selection; individual null-version changes do not affect DQM. Countable Choice supplies L² completeness, separately from density selection.
The tangent set contains scores of designated allowed paths and need not be linear.
The tangent space is the L²-norm closure of the finite real linear span; the empty span is {0}. Countable Choice is assumed.
A nuisance path must be designated and have an existing zero right derivative of the target; exact constancy of the target is not required.
The nuisance orthogonal complement is taken within L²₀(P), with pairing P(hg), rather than within all of L²(P).

load_bearing.statement: Assume the density-version convention for the path in def-dqm-submodel-through-a-law. If s ∈ L²(P) is a DQM score, then Ps=0. Moreover, any two scores satisfying the same DQM expansion agree P-almost surely.
A common-dominated path P_t through P for 0 ≤ t < ε is DQM with score s ∈ L²(P) when the L²(μ) norm of √p_t − √p − (t/2)s√p is o(t) as t decreases to zero.
Assume Countable Choice. For any probability measure P, L²₀(P) is a closed real linear subspace of real L²(P) with pairing ∫fg dP; consequently it is a real Hilbert space.
Assume Countable Choice. The tangent space is the closure in the L²(P) norm of all finite real linear combinations of tangent-set scores; the span of the empty set is {0}.
The nuisance tangent space is the norm closure in L²₀(P) of the finite real linear span of scores of designated allowed DQM paths whose right target derivative exists and is zero.

concerns.concern: The page says it 'fixes the nuisance tangent space by designated paths that hold the target fixed.' The actual Definition in def-nuisance-tangent-space requires only that the right target derivative exist and equal zero. A target can vary at order t² while satisfying that definition. Replace the exact-constancy wording with the zero-first-order-derivative convention.

Common sigma-finite domination, AC selection, individual null-version invariance, and probability-density normalization are preserved. Read the LAN page, its QMD-centering lemma, and def-qmd-path, which is homed on the earlier likelihood-asymptotics page. For a fixed nonzero vector v, h=tv restricts the interior vector QMD expansion to the local one-sided scalar DQM expansion with score vᵀs; v=0 gives the constant path. Neither definition assumes centering. The supplied-density QMD convention and the local AC selection convention remain distinguishable; no boundary or LAN consequence is claimed from scalar DQM alone.

Read the downstream page and its five item bodies. Efficient-score projection uses the closed nuisance space within L²₀(P).
